1.explanation:
1. We import Carbon’s compiled CSS and React components via CDN to create a simple page.
2. We render a <ContentSwitcher> with two <Switch> tabs (‘All’ and ‘Read’) on a white background.
3. By default, the unselected tab gets a #f4f4f4 fill and a very light #e0e0e0 divider, which measures only ~1.1:1 contrast against the white page background—failing WCAG 1.4.11.
4. You can open this page in any browser, inspect the unselected tab’s background and border colors, and verify the contrast ratio with any contrast analyzer tool to reproduce the reported failure.
1.bug_scenario: A default Carbon ContentSwitcher with two tabs (“All” selected, “Read” unselected) renders the unselected tab with a light-grey background (#f4f4f4) and a very light divider stroke (#e0e0e0). When placed on a white page background, that stroke and background combination fails the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast requirement (measured ≈1.1:1 against white), making it difficult to perceive the two buttons as part of a single component.
